title: Numerals 8: Mixed Review in Context
description: Bring lessons 1-7 together: the 1 / 2-4 / 5+ split, compound numbers, numerals in non-nominative cases, collective numerals, and money / age / time, all in realistic sentences.
descriptionRussian: Собираем уроки 1-7 воедино: правило 1 / 2-4 / 5+, составные числительные, числительные в косвенных падежах, собирательные числительные и деньги / возраст / время — всё в реальных предложениях.
intro: The full counting system in one place. Read the last word of the number, pick one of three slots, and check whether the phrase is sitting in a case that makes the number decline too. The teens are the only thing that lies to you about which slot it belongs in.
rules: The last word of a number sets the slot: один → nominative singular, 2-4 → genitive singular, 5+ → genitive plural (двадцать одна книга, двадцать две книги, двадцать пять книг).
The teens 11-14 always count as 5+: одиннадцать книг, тринадцать рублей.
In a non-nominative case the number declines with the noun: к двум часам, с тремя друзьями, о пяти книгах.
Collective numerals двое / трое / четверо take the genitive plural for groups of people, children, and plural-only nouns: двое детей, трое суток.
Money / age / time follow the same split, with the irregular пять ЛЕТ and the dative person for age: два часа, сто рублей, ему пять лет.
examples: В классе двадцать один ученик. (There are twenty-one pupils in the class.) last word 1 → nominative singular ученик.
Я купил три книги и заплатил сто рублей. (I bought three books and paid a hundred roubles.) 3 → книги, the 5+ slot → рублей.
Приходи к двум часам. (Come by two o'clock.) non-nominative: к + dative двум часам.
Лена пришла с тремя подругами. (Lena came with three friends.) non-nominative: с + instrumental тремя подругами.
У них двое детей и трое внуков. (They have two children and three grandchildren.) collectives + genitive plural.
Моему деду восемьдесят два года. (My grandfather is eighty-two.) last word 2 → года; dative деду.
Мы говорили о пяти новых учениках. (We talked about five new pupils.) non-nominative: о + prepositional пяти учениках.

rows.label: 1 / 2-4 / 5+ split
cells: одна книга, две книги, пять книг

rows.label: Compound (last word rules)
cells: двадцать одна книга, двадцать пять книг

items.promptEnglish: There are twenty-one pupils in the class.
items.hint: Read the last word of the compound number.
items.explanation: The last word, один, puts the phrase in the 1 slot, so the noun is the nominative singular: двадцать один ученик. The teens-exception does not apply (this is 21, not 11).

items.prompt: Я купил три книги и заплатил сто _____.
items.promptEnglish: I bought three books and paid a hundred roubles.
items.explanation: Сто (100) is in the 5+ slot, so the noun is the genitive plural рублей. (The first half of the sentence shows три книги: 3 → genitive singular.)

items.hint: к governs the dative; the number itself declines.
items.explanation: In a non-nominative case the number declines too. К takes the dative, and the dative of два is двум: к двум часам. This is the non-nominative-case skill from Lesson 5.

items.hint: Counting children calls for which kind of numeral?
items.explanation: Children are counted with the collective numeral двое plus the genitive plural: двое детей. This is the collective-numeral skill from Lesson 6.

items.hint: Last word два → the 2-4 slot for год.
items.explanation: The compound ends in два (2-4 slot), so the noun is the genitive singular года: восемьдесят два года. Лет is only for the 5+ slot. Age uses the dative person: деду.

items.promptEnglish: We talked about five new pupils.
items.hint: о + prepositional, and the whole phrase agrees.
items.explanation: The preposition о governs the prepositional case, so the whole phrase shifts: о пяти новых учениках. The number (пяти), the adjective (новых), and the noun (учениках) all take the prepositional plural. This is whole-phrase agreement from Lesson 5.

blanks: Лена пришла с _____ подругами. (Lena came with three friends.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: С ('together with') governs the instrumental, so the number declines: the instrumental of три is тремя, with the noun in the instrumental plural: с тремя подругами.

errorCorrection.explanation: In a compound number only the last word decides, and this one ends in две, so the noun follows the 2-4 rule and takes the genitive singular: двадцать две книги. Книг is the genitive plural, correct only when the number ends in 5-9 or 0 (двадцать пять книг). The big front part двадцать never changes the noun; only the final две does.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are three children in the family.
errorCorrection.explanation: Counting children calls for a collective numeral, and after a collective the noun is the genitive plural детей: трое детей. The ordinary три would force the genitive singular ребёнка (три ребёнка), so 'три детей' mixes the two systems and is wrong. Трёх and троих are non-nominative forms (genitive or accusative) used when the phrase leaves the subject slot (у трёх детей). In the nominative subject position here, the form is трое.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: She is friends with three girls.
errorCorrection.explanation: When the whole phrase is in a non-nominative case, the number declines with the noun. The preposition с takes the instrumental, so девочки becomes девочками and три must become тремя: с тремя девочками. Plain три is the frozen nominative-accusative and cannot stand after с. Both halves carry the case, never just the noun.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There are thirty-one books in the library.
minimalPairs.explanation: The compound ends in одна, so the phrase is in the 1 slot: тридцать одна книга (nominative singular). Книг (genitive plural) would only follow a 5+ number like тридцать пять.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He arrived with two children (с + instrumental).
minimalPairs.explanation: Here the phrase is in the instrumental after с, so the ordinary number declines: с двумя детьми. The collective двое is a nominative/accusative form; in the instrumental you use двумя with the noun in the instrumental plural.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each phrase by which numeral skill it tests.

reviewVocab.definition: the core counting rule, set by the last word of the number: один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей.
reviewVocab.example: Двадцать одна книга, двадцать две книги, двадцать пять книг.

reviewVocab.definition: in non-nominative cases the number declines with the noun: к двум, с тремя, о пяти.
collective numerals for groups, children, and plural-only nouns, always with the genitive plural.
reviewVocab.example: У них двое детей и трое внуков.
